title: Auto Loans: Payoff Amount, Payoff Quotes and Lien Release
content:
This policy defines what it takes to pay an Auto Loans account off in full, what a payoff quote states, what happens to an overpayment or a shortfall, and how quickly Piedmont Crescent Bank releases its lien.

## Payoff amount and quotes

For any given date, the payoff amount adds together the unpaid principal, the interest accrued up to and including that date, and the fees due. A payoff quote gives that amount for a date no further ahead than the product's quote validity period, in calendar days, together with the per-diem interest. The per-diem figure equals one day's interest on the unpaid principal: principal times the APR as a hundredth, apportioned over the product's day count, then rounded half-up to the cent.

## Posting a payoff

A payment equal to or greater than the payoff amount for the day it is credited is posted as a payoff. It brings fees, interest and principal down to nothing, and the loan's status becomes paid off. Any excess is returned to the payer within 5 business days by the same means it arrived. A payment short of the payoff amount leaves the loan open and is applied in the ordinary way.

## Lien release

The bank's release of its lien must go out within the product's lien release period, a number of business days measured from the payoff. For this count a business day is any Monday to Friday other than a Federal Reserve holiday. The count starts with the first business day after the closing date as day 1, and the release is due no later than the business day on which the count ends. An electronic title is released by electronic notice to the state's motor vehicle agency; a title that is not electronic is signed and mailed to the borrower's address of record.

Where GAP coverage is still in force at payoff, the payoff gives rise to a GAP refund under the GAP refund rules.

## Illustrations (hypothetical)

**Overpayment.** A payoff amount of 8000.00 met by a payment of 8050.00 leaves 50.00 to be returned to the payer, by the method used, within 5 business days.

**Shortfall.** A payment of 7900.00 against the same payoff amount does not pay the loan off; it is applied as an ordinary payment and the loan stays open.

**Counting business days.** A loan closed on a Friday starts its count on the following Monday as day 1; if that Monday is a Federal Reserve holiday, day 1 is the Tuesday instead, and Saturdays and Sundays are never counted.
